sarah_finance: Heads-up — GCP reseller statement for Feb shows an "unallocated credit" of $12,450. Link: https://console.cloud.google.com/billing/STATEMENT/ABC123 (internal)

leo_ops: Ugh. Do we have any reseller-level refunds/adjusts that would explain that? or a duplicate registration across projects? :thinking_face:

sarah_finance: Not that I can find in our internal ledger. The line item on the statement is weirdly labeled: `MarketplaceCommissionAdjustment` and region is `asia-east1` but our committed usage for that reseller is all `us-west1` for this period.

emma_cloud: Do you have the raw line item ID? I can cross-check against billing export. Might be a mapping issue where GCP attributes marketplace credits to the smallest project in the reseller account.

sarah_finance: Here's the CSV row from the statement (redacted):
```
line_item_id,description,amount,currency,region,reseller_id
LI-597213,MarketplaceCommissionAdjustment,-12450,USD,asia-east1,RS-9082
```

leo_ops: If it's negative (credit) applied to asia-east1 but our committed reservations are tied to different project/reseller mapping, that would explain the reconciliation gap. Could be a channel partner applied a credit to the wrong sub-account.

billingbot: Automated alert: detected mismatch between marketplace_statement.total_credits and ledger.applied_credits for Feb. Delta: $12,450. Case suggested: ENABLE_MANUAL_RECONCILE.

raj_engineering: Quick check — do we have any cross-region cost allocation rules that rewrite the region label in the export? I remember a transformation in the gcp-billing-export pipeline that normalizes region tags. Might have introduced `asia-*` mapping for some legacy SKUs.

emma_cloud: Run this bq query against the exported billing dataset to find all MarketplaceCommissionAdjustment rows from Feb: 
```
SELECT invoice_month, service, sku, usage_start_time, cost FROM `redwood_billing.gcp_export.*` WHERE invoice_month = '2026-02' AND LOWER(description) LIKE '%marketplacecommissionadjustment%'
```

leo_ops: I'll run it now and drop the raw rows in #eng-infra.

sarah_finance: Also note the reseller_id on the statement is RS-9082 — that maps to PartnerCorp via the reseller roster. PartnerCorp told sales they issued a one-time promotional credit in APAC for a pilot, but sales says they asked for it to be applied to their test project, not the production reseller account.

emma_cloud: That explains the region mismatch. Sounds like PartnerCorp submitted the credit with the wrong project/reseller identifier. We need to ask GCP marketplace ops to remap the credit to the correct sub-account or issue a reversing adjustment.

leo_ops: Next steps: 1) export raw statement lines and the matching ledger entries (finance), 2) run BQ query to find any transformed region labels (infra), 3) open GCP support case (cloud) with evidence, 4) ask PartnerCorp for confirmation. I'll own step 2.

sarah_finance: I'll open the finance ticket and include the CSV row + sales note. Ticket: FIN-2026-48. Tagging @sales for visibility.

raj_engineering: FYI, if we anticipate this will be recurring, we should add a check in the monthly reconcile job to flag marketplace credits that don't match reserved capacity IDs by region/reseller. Could avoid manual chasing.

sarah_finance: Agreed. For now, opening support case with GCP and asking PartnerCorp to confirm the intended target. Will post case number once created. :eyes:

billingbot: Support case template: PROVIDE: statement_pdf, csv_row(s), ledger_journal_ids, reseller_mapping_table. Suggested priority: HIGH for revenue-impacting credits.

emma_cloud: If GCP confirms it's their side, request a remap OR a compensating invoice. Keep copies of all evidence; their typical SLA for marketplace adjustments is ~10 business days.

leo_ops: Uploaded BQ export snippet to #eng-infra. Found 3 additional `MarketplaceCommissionAdjustment` lines across Feb with small credits that matched, only RS-9082 was the large one.

sarah_finance: Thanks. I'll draft the support case now and ping PartnerCorp for confirmation. Will update thread when case number exists. :thumbsup:
